blocks.text: The nitrogen cycle is the process by which nitrogen circulates between the biotic and abiotic parts of an ecosystem: atmospheric nitrogen (N2) is changed into compounds that living things can use and is later returned to the air. It runs through five steps.

items: Nitrogen fixation: the air is 78% N2, whose atoms are held by a strong triple bond that plants cannot break; fixation converts N2 to compounds such as ammonia (NH3).

Nitrification: soil bacteria change ammonia, which is toxic or hard for plants to use in large amounts: Nitrosomonas turns ammonia into nitrite (NO2-) and Nitrobacter turns nitrite into nitrate (NO3-), which plants absorb easily.
Assimilation: plants and microbes absorb nitrate and use it to make proteins, DNA and chlorophyll; animals get nitrogen by eating plants and other animals.
Ammonification: when organisms die or animals release nitrogenous wastes, decomposers (fungi and bacteria) break down the proteins and turn organic nitrogen back into ammonia.
Denitrification: in waterlogged soils denitrifying bacteria such as Pseudomonas and Thiobacillus turn nitrate back into N2, which returns to the air.

blocks.caption: Three ways nitrogen is fixed
rows: soil microbes: free-living (cyanobacteria, Azotobacter, Clostridium) and symbiotic (Rhizobium in root nodules of legumes such as chana and moong)
lightning combines N2 with oxygen into nitrogen oxides, then nitrates
N2 and hydrogen combined into ammonia to make fertilisers

blocks.alt: Nitrogen gas (in atmosphere) is fixed by nitrogen-fixing bacteria in the root nodules of a pod-bearing plant and in soil, giving ammonium. Plants feed animals (a rabbit); both go to decomposer bacteria and fungi, which form ammonium (ammonification). Nitrifying bacteria make nitrites and then nitrates (nitrification). Nitrates go to plants (assimilation) or, through denitrifying bacteria, back to nitrogen gas (denitrification).

blocks.title: Tidbit
blocks.text: While the water cycle moves a substance we can see, the nitrogen cycle deals with an invisible gas that makes up about 78% of our atmosphere.
